thread:
oscar-cs: Heads up — HearthCare just flagged a big drop in retrieval+rerank quality after last night's rerank rollout. They say citations are missing and recall on our medical QA prompts is ~30% down. They pasted a short repro and sample responses. Can we triage?

maria-cs: Ugh. Got the ticket (HC-4721). Customer included before/after outputs and topk=10 request logs. They report: previously 8/10 correct citations, now 3/10.

oscar-cs: Pasted payload they sent (redacted IDs):
```json
{
  "endpoint": "/v1/retrieve_and_rerank",
  "query": "What are the contraindications for Drug X in pregnancy?",
  "top_k": 10,
  "reranker": "rr-v2-global",
  "context_sources": ["internal-kb:hc-guidelines", "pubmed-index"],
  "trace_id": "hc-2026-02-09-xyz"
}
```

liam-ml: Did they specify embeddings model used for retrieval? RR changes shouldn't drop recall unless inputs changed or recall threshold/score normalization was updated.

maria-cs: They said embeddings=embed-med-1 (same as before). Only change was reranker switch to `rr-v2-global` in the staged rollout.

aj-devex: Hmm. Can we reproduce locally? Trying a curl with their payload now. If we can reproduce we should isolate whether retrieval vs rerank is the problem. Suggest call sequence: retrieve (topk 50) -> rerank locally with rr-v1/rr-v2 -> compare scores.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: Finished rollout: `rerank/rr-v2-global` -> 100% traffic @ 2026-02-09T03:24:12Z.

emily-prod: Quick note — we also landed a change to prefix-KV caching that might be trimming duplicate docs earlier in the pipeline (it was intended to reduce token cost). Could be dropping supporting docs before rerank. Rollout window aligns.

liam-ml: Good catch. That would manifest as fewer candidates reaching the reranker (so downstream recall drop). @aj-devex can you fetch the raw retrieval results (pre-cache) for their trace_id? If pre-cache shows 10 relevant docs but post-cache only 4, caching is it.

aj-devex: Got logs for trace hc-2026-02-09-xyz: pre-cache candidates=48, post-cache candidates=9. Looks like dedup/merge threshold was too aggressive for medical citations (many short overlapping abstracts got collapsed).

oscar-cs: Customer included before/after model outputs to compare. Before (rr-v1 + no-cache): included PubMed PMID:12345 and guidelines doc. After: those docs missing, output says "No known contraindications" — which is incorrect for Drug X. They're pretty upset, requesting rollback or hotfix.

liam-ml: Plan: immediate remediation — (1) pin HearthCare traffic to rr-v1 and bypass prefix-caching for their org; (2) patch caching heuristics (lower dedup threshold) and run small canary; (3) run regression eval on medical prompt suite. I'll take 1 and 2.

maria-cs: Please confirm ETA so I can update the customer. They're pacing the call in 60m.

liam-ml: ETA ~45m to pin + bypass for their org. Command to split traffic: `infra traffic-split set --service rerank --version rr-v1 --org HearthCare --weight 100` — running now.

sre-bot: incident-bot: Created incident INC-2026-78: "HearthCare retrieval/rerank regression after rr-v2 rollout". Severity P1 (customer-impact).

aj-devex: Traffic split succeeded. HearthCare now on rr-v1 + caching-bypass. Re-testing their sample now.

aj-devex: Repro check: with rr-v1 & bypass — returned PubMed PMID:12345 and guidelines doc, reranker top result relevance score 0.87. Looks like immediate improvement.

oscar-cs: Passed to customer. They confirmed in-thread: "We're seeing the expected citations again. Thanks for the quick action."

emily-prod: Will open a follow-up PR to adjust dedup threshold and add a targeted canary for medical corpora. Also adding a per-org caching opt-out flag for urgent rollbacks.

liam-ml: After patch and canary we'll schedule a controlled re-roll of rr-v2 with new caching heuristics. Also running regression suite against HC's eval set.

maria-cs: Marking HC ticket as "mitigated" pending customer confirmation tomorrow AM. Thanks team.

oscar-cs: Thanks all. Quick notes for postmortem: correlate rerank rollout + caching change, poor canary coverage on medical domain, need per-org opt-out, add alert for post-rollout recall regression on high-sensitivity customers.

liam-ml: Adding to INC-2026-78 timeline and will own the postmortem.

oscar-cs: Closing thread for now — will update when postmortem is ready.
